Based on my analysis:

**Test image observations:**
- Mature soybean pods, brown to dark brown coloration
- Pods appear somewhat shriveled/irregular on dry stems
- Multiple pods showing dark brown discoloration throughout
- No white mold, no obvious leaf spots — pod/stem focused

**Reference comparison:**
- **Anthracnose**: Top-right panel shows very similar brown dry pods on dry stems — closest visual match
- **Phomopsis**: Shows distinctive circular pycnidia spots on pods — not clearly visible here
- **Diaporthe**: Shows linear pycnidia on stems — stems here look uniformly dry
- **Charcoal_Rot**: Stem-focused with gray coloration — doesn't match
- **Tobacco_Streak_Virus**: Shows opened pods with discolored seeds — different pattern

The brown, dry, irregularly discolored pods on brown stems most closely resemble the Anthracnose reference imagery. Anthracnose causes "brown irregularly shaped spots on pods" and "pod blanking," consistent with the shriveled/dark appearance seen here.
